d.t: Used to express the speaker's wish that the preceding statement were true.
d.e: - I don't know how I'm going to afford all these Christmas presents. - Maybe you'll win the lottery and become a millionaire overnight. - I wish!

d.t: A form of mild swearing used to emphasize the truth of an assertion; accompanied by if and the opposite of the assertion.
d.e: It's a joke — if it isn't, I wish I may be shot.

d.t: Used to denote that the speaker finds another person sexually attractive.
d.e: Look at that chick hanging out by the entrance. — I would!

d.t: Used to show that the speaker hates or strongly dreads the task in question.
d.e: I would rather die than hear that awful song again.
